blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it

findings.recommendation: Flatten without changing behavior: `continue` early on an empty email and on an unchanged plan, merge the two seat conditions into one filter, and move the seat loop into a helper so `import` reads as "find or create the account, then add its new seats".
findings.title: `import` nests six levels deep

findings.recommendation: Extract one helper, e.g. `add_new_seats(db, account_id, existing, seats) -> Result<usize, DbError>`, used by both the `Some` and `None` arms, so the seat filter lives in a single place.
findings.title: Seat-adding loop duplicated in both match arms

findings.recommendation: A reader without the plan cannot tell whether skipping new seats on an account whose plan is unchanged is intended or a bug; the proposal only says "creates missing accounts and their seats". State the rule in a comment (or confirm it is a defect), and note that the account's plan itself is never updated here either.
findings.title: Seats are only added to an existing account when its plan differs, without saying why

findings.recommendation: Name the checks (e.g. `fn looks_like_email(seat: &str) -> bool`) and say in a comment why rows without an email and seats without '@' are dropped silently rather than reported; `seats: Vec<String>` could also document that a seat is an email address.
findings.title: Unexplained filters: `contains('@')` and empty email skip silently

findings.evidence: - [x] 1.1 `import`, verified by importing last month's CSV export on staging
findings.recommendation: Add tests named after the behavior (creates a missing account with its seats, adds only new seats to an existing account, skips rows without an email, ignores seats without '@') so a newcomer can learn the rules from them; today the only verification is a manual staging run.
findings.title: No test describes the import behavior
